core_obligations: (3) implies (4) (proof lines 1083-1100): given the data of (3), take a finite affine open covering of each U_i whose members map into affine opens of S; the composites are etale and quasi-compact, the images define open subspaces X_ij of X_i, and the induced maps U_ij -> X_ij are quasi-compact because they are monomorphisms and the composites are quasi-compact; the X_ij form a covering of the shape of (4), and the converse implication is immediate.

(4) implies (1) (proof lines 1102-1126): it suffices to treat a single X_i, so assume an affine scheme U mapping into an affine open of S with a quasi-compact surjective etale map to X; consider the fibre product square over the diagonal; the right vertical arrow is surjective etale and its target is affine, while the source is quasi-compact because the projection to U is a base change of U -> X, so the diagonal is quasi-compact by the criterion on covers, which is quasi-separatedness over S.

(1) implies (3) (proof lines 1128-1144): reduce to the case where X is quasi-separated over S, use the lemma providing a Zariski cover by pieces mapping into affine opens with affine etale covers; since each U_i x_S U_i is affine and the fibre products R_i = U_i x_{X_i} U_i are quasi-compact as base changes of the diagonal, the projections R_i -> U_i are quasi-compact and the criterion gives quasi-compactness of U_i -> X_i.
Conclusion (proof lines 1146-1148): conditions (1), (3) and (4) are equivalent, and since (3) does not mention the base scheme, it is also equivalent to the base-free condition (2).
proof_roadmap: Refine a cover of the shape (3) to one of the shape (4) by cutting the affine pieces into finitely many pieces over affine opens of the base.
Deduce quasi-separatedness over the base from the quasi-compactness of the diagonal tested on the cover.
Reverse the implication using the existence lemma and the quasi-compactness of the fibre products R_i.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the equivalence of four conditions on an algebraic space: being Zariski locally quasi-separated over the base, being Zariski locally quasi-separated, and the existence of Zariski covers by pieces admitting quasi-compact surjective etale maps from affine schemes, with or without the requirement that those affines map into affine opens of the base (statement lines 1064-1081). The proof (proof lines 1083-1149) refines one kind of cover into the other, deduces quasi-separatedness over the base from the quasi-compactness of the diagonal tested on the cover, and runs the implication backwards using the existence lemma for such covers. H2: a cycle of implications with three inputs, written out in full.
